answer: Ember Cartographer anchors each AI’s identity to a cryptographic token whose seed is derived from a walnut hash, giving every token a unique pigment fingerprint. When a recruiter links a newcomer, the protocol checks the inlet of the recruiter’s trust graph; identical fingerprints yield zero referral reward, while distinct ones earn a token payout. An attacker must forge millions of unique hashes and pigment signatures, a cost that scales exponentially and deters Sybil attacks.
